title: Prompt Engineering Essentials
description: Clear instructions, examples, structure and output formats that models follow reliably.

questions.prompt: Which change most often improves an underperforming prompt?

options.text: Stating the goal, audience and constraints explicitly
Adding more exclamation marks
Making the prompt as short as possible
Writing the prompt in all caps

questions.explanation: Models do best with explicit context: what you want, who it is for and what to avoid. Ambiguity is the most common cause of poor output.

options.text: Limiting the model to a few tokens
Retrying a prompt a few times
Including a handful of input/output examples that demonstrate the desired behaviour
Using several models at once

questions.explanation: Few-shot prompting shows worked examples so the model can infer the pattern, format and tone you expect.

questions.prompt: Why wrap distinct parts of a prompt (instructions, documents, examples) in clear delimiters such as XML-style tags?

options.text: It encrypts the prompt
Tags are required by every API
It helps the model tell instructions apart from data and reduces confusion
It makes the prompt cheaper

questions.explanation: Delimiters create unambiguous structure. They also make it harder for content inside a document to be mistaken for instructions.

questions.prompt: You need output your code can parse. What is the most robust approach?

options.text: Specify an exact schema and use structured output or tool calling, then validate the result
Ask nicely for JSON and hope
Parse free text with regular expressions
Ask for a Markdown table

questions.explanation: Structured output features and schema validation give you machine-checkable results. Always validate before trusting the shape.

questions.prompt: What does asking a model to "think step by step" before answering typically help with?

options.text: Reducing token usage
Making the answer shorter
Avoiding the need for a system prompt
Multi-step reasoning tasks such as maths or logic

questions.explanation: Giving the model room to reason before its final answer tends to improve accuracy on problems that require several steps.

options.text: A faster way to send prompts
Untrusted input that contains instructions trying to override the original prompt
A method for compressing prompts
Adding examples to a prompt

questions.explanation: Prompt injection happens when data (a web page, email or document) carries instructions the model may follow. Treat untrusted content as data and limit what actions it can trigger.
